from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Observe the squirrel gathering nuts over time.",
            "Derivative shows instantaneous nut-gathering speed.",
            "Integral calculates total nuts collected."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Motion Analogy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(t * 2) + 0.5, x_range=[0, 3], color=WHITE)
        point = Dot(color="#FF00FF")
        label = Text("Position at time t", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        tangent = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B1", "E6")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.place_at_grid(point, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        self.place_at_grid(label, "B3")
        self.play(Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(tangent, "C3")
        self.play(Create(tangent))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        area =  self.place_in_area(VMobject(), "C1", "E6")
        area.set_fill("#FFFF00", opacity=0.3)
        area.set_stroke(opacity=0)
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Derivatives act like a zoom lens.", "They reveal slope at any point.", "Imagine the rocket's vertical velocity."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Derivative: The Slope Inspector", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Curve
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**3, color=WHITE)
        
        # Points and Secant
        p1 = ValueTracker(1.0)
        p2 = ValueTracker(3.0)
        
        def get_point(t): return axes.c2p(t, 0.2 * t**3)
        
        dot1 = Dot(get_point(p1.get_value()), color=YELLOW)
        dot2 = Dot(get_point(p2.get_value()), color=YELLOW)
        
        secant = always_redraw(lambda: Line(get_point(p1.get_value()), get_point(p2.get_value()), color=YELLOW))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(curve))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(dot1), FadeIn(dot2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(secant))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Shrink the gap
        self.play(p2.animate.set_value(1.1), run_time=3)
        self.play(FadeOut(dot2), FadeOut(secant))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Integral: The Area Accumulator", ["Integrals accumulate small, infinitesimal parts.", "We stack rectangles to find area.", "This sums flow into total volume."])
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2*x**2 + 1, x_range=[0, 3], color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, curve), 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 3], color="#00FF00", opacity=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[0, 3], dx=0.2, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(area, rects))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem: The Inverse Relationship", 
                          ["Integration reverses the differentiation process.", 
                           "It acts like an undo button.", 
                           "Differentiating an integral restores the function."])
        
        f_prime = MathTex(r"f'(x)", color="#FF5733")
        f_int = MathTex(r"F(x) = \int f(t) dt", color="#33FF57")
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(f_prime, "B2", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(f_int, "D2", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"), Write(f_prime))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"), Write(f_int), GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33CCFF"), Indicate(f_prime), Indicate(f_int))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", ["Differentiation breaks motion into rates.", "Integration builds position from rates.", "They form a perfect mathematical cycle."])
        
        # Create visual elements
        func = Text("f(x)", color=BLUE)
        deriv = Text("f'(x)", color=YELLOW)
        
        # Grid positions
        self.place_at_grid(func, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(deriv, "B5")
        
        arrow_diff = Arrow(self.grid["B2"] + RIGHT*0.5, self.grid["B5"] + LEFT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        arrow_integ = Arrow(self.grid["B5"] + DOWN*0.5 + LEFT*0.5, self.grid["B2"] + DOWN*0.5 + RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        
        diff_label = Text("Derivative", font_size=16, color=YELLOW).next_to(arrow_diff, UP, buff=0.1)
        integ_label = Text("Integral", font_size=16, color=GREEN).next_to(arrow_integ, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        cycle = VGroup(func, deriv, arrow_diff, arrow_integ, diff_label, integ_label)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), FadeIn(func), FadeIn(arrow_diff), FadeIn(diff_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN), FadeIn(deriv), FadeIn(arrow_integ), FadeIn(integ_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), Indicate(cycle))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Motion Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the concept using a squirrel gathering nuts. The derivative represents the instantaneous speed (rate of change of nut-gathering), while the integral represents the total count of nuts gathered over time. Prerequisites: Basic understanding of velocity and distance.
sections.example: A squirrel's velocity graph shows peaks and valleys; the area under this curve corresponds exactly to the total nuts collected.

sections.title: Visualizing the Derivative: The Slope Inspector
sections.content: Visualize the derivative as a 'magnifying glass' zooming into a curve to find its instantaneous slope. Use an animation of a tangent line moving along a trajectory curve.
sections.example: If a rocket's altitude function is h(t), the derivative h'(t) gives the slope, which visually represents the rocket's vertical velocity at any specific frame.

sections.title: Visualizing the Integral: The Area Accumulator
sections.content: Introduce the integral as 'stacking' infinitesimal rectangles to find the total area under a curve. Use animation where rectangles fill the space under a path to represent accumulation.
sections.example: Imagine a conveyor belt filling a container; the integral 'sums' the infinitesimal slices of flow to calculate the final volume in the container.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: The Inverse Relationship
sections.content: The core realization: Integration is the reverse operation of differentiation. Show the 'Undo' button visual effect. Explain that differentiating an integral returns the original function.
sections.example: If you derive the position, you get velocity. If you integrate velocity, you get back to position (plus a constant). They are mathematical 'opposites' that cancel each other out.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude by unifying the concepts: Differentiation breaks down the whole into rates of change, while integration builds the whole from those rates. A final graphic shows a cycle: Function -> (Derivative) -> Rate -> (Integral) -> Function.
sections.example: A robot's path: Differentiation tells the robot how to turn (steering angle), Integration tells the robot where it is in the world (positioning).
